value.rationale: The first dyadic lacunary three-level real subspace is the smallest natural geometric six-frequency test case with a three-frequency fourth-order additive resonance, important for comparing real and analytic sparse Fourier norm geometry. Rather than a single computed point, the work provides a complete sharp L4/L2 interval, phase and modulus rigidity, two explicit quantitative nonnegative deficits, and a generic-gap phase boundary with sharp higher-gap bounds. These exact norm invariants and stability forms have plausible use for sparse trigonometric approximation and small-dimensional harmonic design; general estimates do not deliver them. Ternary examples establish a genuine boundary rather than an arbitrary finite slice.
